title: Cable stripe baby blanket
subtitle: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket alternating cable columns and garter stripe panels.
excerpt: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket in aran weight on 5 mm needles. Five vertical panels alternate: a six-stitch cable column, a twelve-stitch garter panel, a six-stitch cable column, a twelve-stitch garter panel, and a six-stitch cable column. About 300 g of aran.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 10th series (1894), §Cable and Rib Nursery Wraps, gives a striped cable panel cot blanket in aran weight. The six-stitch cable-front crossing is documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Cable Stitches.

knitting.gaugeText: 18 sts × 24 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 5 mm needles. Cable panels draw in by about 2 sts per cable column.

glossaryTerms.definition: A left-crossing six-stitch cable. Slip 3 stitches to a cable needle and hold to the front of the work, knit the next 3 stitches from the left needle, then knit the 3 stitches from the cable needle. The column spirals to the left.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 5 mm needles. Six-stitch cable columns alternate with garter-stitch panels. Finished size: 75 cm wide by 90 cm long.

Single-panel construction; no seaming. Three cable columns are separated by two twelve-stitch garter panels. Garter-stitch panels were chosen as the filler because they lie perfectly flat next to cables, require no border treatment, and make the cable columns stand out clearly. Cable spacing every 8 rows gives a crisp, regular spiral. Budget about 300 g (about 530 m / 580 yards) of aran. Buy in matched dye lots.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 300 g (about 530 m / 580 yards) of aran-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 5 mm (UK 6 / US 8) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

18 stitches and 24 rows to 10 cm in garter stitch on 5 mm needles. Each six-stitch cable column draws in by about 2 stitches relative to an equivalent garter panel, so the cast-on count is adjusted for this: 153 total stitches gives a finished width of approximately 75 cm.
If your garter gauge is 16 per 10 cm with 153 stitches, the blanket will be about 84 cm wide.
Stitches used

items.name: C6F
items.qty: cable 6 front: sl3 to cable needle hold front, k3, k3 from cable needle

content.text: Pattern
Cast-on

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 153 stitches: [3 edge] + [6 cable] + [12 garter] + [6 cable] + [12 garter] + [6 cable] + [3 edge] = 48 core stitches + 3 edge each side + 5 extra to adjust for cable draw-in = 153. Place markers after the 3rd, 9th, 21st, 27th, 39th, and 45th stitches counting from each edge to mark each cable panel. Long-tail tail: (5 × 153) / 10 + 15 = 76.5 + 15 = 92 cm. Measure 105 cm.
Body
RS rows (non-cable): k3, k6, k12, k6, k12, k6, k3.
RS cable rows (every 8 rows, starting at row 5): k3,
C6F
WS rows: k all stitches. (Garter stitch on both faces; cable columns show on RS.)
Continue until the blanket measures 90 cm. When you set this aside, note whether the next cable row is due and which row of the 8-row cycle you are on.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 108 (about 45 cm): count across. You should have 153 stitches. At row 214 (about 89 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults
Cable crossing to the right instead of left: C6F hold was to the back instead of the front. The cable needle must be in front of the work before knitting the first 3 stitches from the main needle.
Cables crossing every 4 rows instead of 8, giving a rope-twist look rather than a wide-twist cable: the row counter was not advanced correctly. Use a sticky note to mark the cable row number.
Cast-off
Cast off knitwise with a relaxed tension. A cable cast-off can be tight; go up one needle size if needed.
Finishing
Weave in ends. A light wet block opens the cable columns and squares the garter panels.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash aran. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

From three cable columns, try a full Aran blanket next. Add more panel types: honeycomb, lattice, and rope, separated by seed-stitch columns. The cabling technique is the same; only the variety increases.
